items.text: Every breaker and disconnect is legibly marked with the load it actually serves; directory matches the house as wired, no live circuit labelled spare.
Non-dwelling service equipment carries the available fault current field marking (110.24 does not mandate it at dwelling services) with the calculation date; calculation is in the job folder.
Breaker interrupting ratings (kAIC) equal or exceed the available fault current at the service.
Working space in front of the panel is at least 3 ft deep (Condition 1), 30 in wide or equipment width if greater, and 6-1/2 ft high, measured from the face of the equipment.
Working space is completely clear — no storage, no water heater, no shelving — and stays clear at final.
Dedicated space above the panel (footprint, up to 6 ft or ceiling) has no foreign piping, ducts or other trades' systems passing through.
Illumination at the panel works and lights the working space.
Every unused opening in panel, boxes and enclosures is closed with a listed blank or plug — no tape, no open knockouts.
All terminations torqued to the panel/equipment label value with a torque tool; values checked after all conductors are landed.
Every lug and connector marking matches the conductor metal landed on it (CU, AL-CU or CU-AL as applicable); no CCA or aluminum on a CU-only terminal.
No backstabbed connections except 14 AWG solid copper; no CCA, stranded or 12 AWG on push-in terminals.
Panel and equipment labels and instruction sheets were read and followed; any conflict between habit and instructions was resolved in favor of the instructions.
All new gear — panel, meter-main, breakers, disconnects — is Siemens.
In any existing panel, breakers are the brand listed for that panel only; no mixed brands to fill spaces.
Where the layout is back-to-back (meter outside, panel inside), full 110.26 working space is still clear in front of the panel.
Wire metal confirmed for the job (copper default; CCA one AWG up, aluminum column, AL-CU/CU-AL terminations) before sizing or landing anything.
